newsitem.title: USA: Cache Capital to launch new hedge fund next month.
newsitem.headline: Cache Capital to launch new hedge fund next month.

text.p: The field of hedge funds continues to grow and shows no signs of letting up, as startup Cache Capital Ltd said on Tuesday it will launch a fund on September 1.

The fund's principal investment vehicle will be the private placement of convertible securities by a public company, which offers investors the ability to purchase shares at a discount of 10 to 30 percent of the prevailing market price. Investments will focus on small or micro cap public companies.
The firm plans to cap the fund at $50 million.

Cache Capital's fund is the second to be manged by Joseph Canouse, president and founder of Atlanta-based J.P. Carey Inc, an international investment banking firm formed in early 1995. Canouse also manages Atlantis, a Cayman Island fund that has had a rate of return of 46 percent since its inception in November 1996.
Prior to founding J.P. Carey, Canouse was part of the international sales division at Josephthal, Lyon & Ross.
Cache Capital, based in Bermuda, will be open to U.S. investors through its Deleware unit Cache Capital LP and will have a minimum subscription of $100,000.
